intervals (per LYRIC recommendations) may be considered prior to 
obtaining a biopsy.34 In the case of NLPHL, residual FDG-PET–avid 
disease can represent foci of concurrent or transformed diffuse large 
B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) or reactive lymph node with progressive 
transformation of germinal centers.109,110 

Select Principles of Supportive Care 

Several neurotoxic chemotherapy agents are utilized in the treatment of 
pediatric patients with HL, including Bv, vincristine, and vinblastine, thus 
providers need to be aware of grading and/or screening methods as well 
as appropriate management. 

Although variations exist between institutional protocols, the following 
supportive care issues are important to consider in the treatment of 
pediatric patients with HL. 

Immunotherapy 

Grading and/or screening methods that can be utilized for peripheral 
neuropathy include the Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events 
(CTCAE) v5.0 or Balis Score, patient reported outcomes, or the Pediatric-
modified Total Neuropathy Score (peds-mTNS) and/or the Total 
Neuropathy Score-pediatric version.111,112 

For patients who develop peripheral neuropathy, reducing the dose of or 
holding the neurotoxic chemotherapy agent based on protocol 
recommendations may be considered.113,114 Early referral to physical 
therapy should also be considered. 

Prior to initiating CPI containing regimens, patients and caregivers should 
receive counseling on the wide-ranging warning signs and symptoms of 
immune-related adverse events (irAEs). A thorough clinical assessment is 
also recommended, including physical examination alongside patient and 
relevant family history of autoimmune or organ-specific disease, 
endocrinopathy, or infectious disease. 

To date, no pharmacologic intervention has shown benefit for peripheral 
neuropathy in the pediatric and adolescent cancer population. For patients 
≥18 years of age, consideration can be made for duloxetine. See the 
NCCN Guidelines for Adult Cancer Pain (available at www.NCCN.org) for 
further information. 

A clinical exam with irAE symptom assessment should be performed at 
each visit, assessing for any new signs or symptoms, including severe 
fatigue, headache, rash, cough, shortness of breath, chest pain, 
abdominal bloating, change in bowel pattern, weight loss, vision changes 
or eye pain, severe muscle weakness, severe muscle or joint pains, and/or 
mood changes. 

Risk of Cardiac Toxicity 

A COG study examined long-term outcomes among children with newly 
diagnosed malignancies, including HL, who received dexrazoxane as part 
of clinical trial therapy.115 Patients who had been randomized to 
doxorubicin with or without dexrazoxane were assessed with a median 
follow-up period of 18.6 years. Dexrazoxane was not found to be 
associated with relapse (HR, 0.84), secondary cancers (HR, 1.19), 

Blood work including a CBC, CMP, thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH), 
free thyroxine (T4), and serum cortisol (morning preferred), is 
recommended prior to initiating a CPI-based regimen as well as at regular 
intervals during therapy. For further details on blood work 
recommendations, see Select Principles of Supportive Care in the 
algorithm. For other pre-assessment, monitoring, and irAE management

all-cause mortality (HR, 1.07), or cardiovascular mortality (HR, 1.45), and 
serious cardiovascular outcomes occurred less commonly when 
dexrazoxane was used (5.6% vs 17.6%; P = .02). In a retrospective study 
assessing outcomes among children with HL, acute lymphoblastic 
leukemia, or osteosarcoma who received doxorubicin with or without 
dexrazoxane, the use of dexrazoxane, particularly among those who 
received a cumulative doxorubicin dose of ≥250 mg/m2, was associated 
with a reduced risk of reduction in lower left ventricular function or ejection 
fraction at 18.1 ± 2.7 years from cancer diagnosis.116 

Based on this study, strong consideration should be made for 
administering dexrazoxane to children and adolescents expected to 
receive ≥250 mg/m2 of cumulative doxorubicin, or an equivalent amount of 
an alternative anthracycline.117 

The Panel recommends an interim history and physical examination every 
3 to 4 months for 1 to 2 years, then every 6 to 12 months until year 3, and 
then annually until 5 years. Recommended laboratory studies include: 
CBC with differential, ESR or CRP, and a chemistry profile as clinically 
indicated. If the patient’s neck was treated with RT, TSH should be 
evaluated annually. If patients were exposed to regimens that contain 
bleomycin or pulmonary RT, or have significant pulmonary involvement or 
other clinical concerns, PFTs should be considered. At the end of therapy, 
an echocardiogram may be considered, with repeat echocardiograms 
thereafter based on specific risk profile (eg, Children’s Oncology Group 
Long-Term Follow-up Guidelines). 

An annual influenza vaccination and other vaccines per the Centers for 
Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) is recommended for all patients 
(see the COG Survivorship Guidelines127 for more details). 

For additional select supportive care recommendations, including 
management of Bv-related infusion reactions and growth factor 
recommendations, see Select Principles of Supportive Care in the 
algorithm. Additional growth factor recommendations can also be found in 
the NCCN Guidelines for Hematopoietic Growth Factors (available at 
www.NCCN.org). 

Follow-Up After Completion of Treatment 

Screening for delayed immune-mediate adverse events (IMAE), such as 
hypothyroidism, which may present within the first 2 years following 
completion of treatment, may be needed for those who received a CPI. In 
a retrospective study among 795 patients treated with CPIs, 10.8% of 
IMAEs occurred >12 months after initiation of the CPI, with kidney and 
hematologic IMAEs the most frequent late-onset IMAEs.128 

Given the long-term risks of the therapies for HL, including secondary 
cancers, fatigue, pulmonary toxicity, thyroid dysfunction, and reproductive 
issues,118-126 patients should be followed by an oncologist or survivorship 
specialist who is aware of these risks and complications, in coordination 
with the primary care provider, especially during the first 2 years after 
treatment. The follow-up schedule should be individualized, depending on 
clinical circumstances such as patient’s age, sex, stage of disease, and 
initial treatment modality. It is recommended that the patient be provided 
with a treatment summary at the completion of therapy, including details of 

Due to the risk of false positives, routine or surveillance FDG-PET scans 
are discouraged. If relapse is suspected (based on imaging, clinical, and 
pathologic correlations) imaging studies are recommended. It is 
acceptable to obtain a posterior-anterior and lateral chest x-ray, CT scan 
with contrast, or MRI of original sites of disease, followed at 3- to 6-month 
intervals for up to 2 years following completion of therapy. Although an 
MRI scan may substitute CT scan for neck, abdomen, and pelvic regions,

a diagnostic CT of the chest is required to evaluate lung parenchyma. If 
the previous FDG-PET was positive (Deauville 3 to 5), an FDG-PET/CT or 
FDG-PET/MRI scan is recommended to confirm CR at the end of all 
prescribed therapy, including RT. The Panel notes that once negative, a 
repeat FDG-PET should not be done unless evaluating suspicious findings 
on the history and physical, CT, or MRI. In addition, to minimize 
false-positive results, it is important to wait at least 8 to 12 weeks after the 
end of RT to perform FDG-PET assessments. 

In general, and in terms of monitoring late effects (≥2 years after 
completion of systemic therapy), patients should be encouraged to 
undergo counseling on issues regarding survivorship, long-term treatment 
effects (eg, secondary cancers [with special attention to thyroid and breast 
cancer], cardiac disease, and issues affecting the thyroid, bone, and 
fertility and reproductive health), health habits, and psychosocial issues. 
For comprehensive details, see the COG Survivorship Guidelines.127 

Summary 

Pediatric HL is now curable in most patients because of the introduction of 
more effective and less toxic regimens. However, survivors may 
experience late treatment-related side effects. For this reason, long-term 
follow-up is essential after completion of treatment. In addition, 
improvements in harmonization of staging and response criteria, and risk 
stratification will improve the therapeutic index.10 Emerging data will 
continue to inform the Panel’s recommendations and consistent with 
NCCN philosophy, participation in clinical trials is always encouraged.

age_years.definition: Patient age at diagnosis or at the decision point, in years.

histology.definition: Histologic diagnosis: classic Hodgkin lymphoma (CHL), nodular lymphocyte-predominant Hodgkin lymphoma (NLPHL), or other. Also used for relapse histology.

ann_arbor_stage.definition: Ann Arbor stage as stated in the case. Suffix X denotes bulky mediastinal disease; suffix E denotes extranodal involvement.

extranodal_involvement.definition: True if the case states extranodal involvement (E modifier).

b_symptoms.definition: True if the case states B symptoms (fever, night sweats, or weight loss).

bulky_disease.definition: True if the case states bulky disease as defined by the guideline. The numeric criterion is not reproduced in the source boxes, so this is recorded as the case statement.

risk_factors_present.definition: True if the case states that the patient has one or more of the guideline's early-stage risk factors for classic Hodgkin lymphoma. The individual criteria are not reproduced in the source boxes.

nodal_sites_count.definition: Number of involved nodal sites (single node versus multiple nodes).

resection_status.definition: Extent of surgical resection of the involved node or mass.

stage_confirmed_by_fdg_pet_ct.definition: True if the stage is confirmed by FDG-PET/CT as stated in the case.

recurrent_infections.definition: True if the patient has recurrent infections.

atypical_presentation.definition: True if the presentation is atypical as stated in the case.

immunodeficiency_history.definition: True if the patient has a personal or family history of immunodeficiency.

bleomycin_indicated.definition: Clinician judgement that bleomycin is indicated for this patient's planned regimen.

biopsy_site_of_concern.definition: Clinician judgement that a biopsy site is of concern for relapse or persistent disease.

biopsy_result.definition: Result of a biopsy of the primary site or of a site of concern.

pet_reimaging_result.definition: Overall result of reimaging with FDG-PET/CT or FDG-PET/MRI as stated in the case.

relapse_pet_deauville_score.definition: Deauville score (1 to 5) on FDG-PET/CT or FDG-PET/MRI performed for relapse or restaging.

interim_deauville_score.definition: Deauville score (1 to 5) on interim (early) response FDG-PET/CT.

end_of_therapy_deauville_score.definition: Deauville score (1 to 5) on end-of-therapy (late) response FDG-PET/CT.

clinical_trial_available.definition: Clinician judgement that a relevant clinical trial is available to the patient.

highly_favorable_patient.definition: Clinician judgement that the patient is highly favorable for further therapy.

disease_status.definition: Disease status as stated in the case: newly diagnosed, relapsed after response, or refractory to prior therapy. Relapse or refractory status selects the relapsed-disease workup and re-induction pathway.

relapse_suspected.definition: Clinician judgement that relapse is suspected, so that imaging is recommended during follow-up.

clinical_concern.definition: Clinician judgement that there is clinical concern (for example symptoms or examination findings) for relapse during follow-up.

center_of_expertise_referral.criteria: Refer to or consult with a center of expertise
center_of_expertise_referral.definition: Clinician judgement that the patient has been referred to or consulted with a center of expertise for relapsed or refractory disease.

autoimmune_disease_history.definition: True if the case states active or previously documented autoimmune disease.

immunosuppressive_therapy_current.definition: True if the case states current use of immunosuppressive agents.

chl_stage_group.definition: Stage group for classic Hodgkin lymphoma: stage I-II with or without risk factors, or stage III-IV.

nlphl_stage_group.definition: Treatment group for nodular lymphocyte-predominant Hodgkin lymphoma by stage, resection, bulk, and node count.

early_response_category.definition: Category of interim (early) response by Deauville score.

late_response_category.definition: Category of end-of-therapy (late) response by Deauville score.

end_of_therapy_adequate.definition: True if the end-of-therapy response is adequate (Deauville 1-3).

relapse_pet_deauville_category.definition: Deauville category on relapse or restaging FDG-PET.

cpi_caution_flag.definition: True if the patient has active or previously documented autoimmune disease and/or current use of immunosuppressive agents, in which case checkpoint inhibitors (CPIs) should be used with caution.

notes.predicates: Conditions were drafted and reviewed by a language model (model_reviewed), not by clinicians. 'rejected' means the review rejected the draft; the box then needs clinician judgement. 'section_only' means the box only requires the patient to be in the page's guideline section.
notes.coordinates: bbox and line_bboxes are PDF points with the origin at the page's top left; pages[].size gives the page size.
notes.links: page links name a page id from pages[]; a multi-page code such as PROS-F has ids 'PROS-F 1 of 5' ... ; external_guideline links name another guideline's slug.
notes.reextracted_pages: Pages listed in quality.reextracted_pages were typed as footnote pages (or had no boxes) although they hold flowcharts. Their boxes, arrows and conditions were written from the PDF page by a language-model reviewer (data/<slug>/page_specs/<page>.json, nccn_nav.page_spec) and are not clinician-validated; arrows are image_checked, conditions model_reviewed or none. pages[].kind_before keeps the earlier kind.
